De acuerdo. Como el orden no está prescrito y usted sugiere P1, fijo la especificación con elementos vectoriales Lagrange de primer orden (P1) sobre la malla de 64 elementos por borde. Con esto el requerimiento está completo.


Use FEniCS legacy (dolfin).
Solve small-strain linear elasticity as a 2D plane-stress variational problem with a direct linear solver.
Geometry: L-shaped domain equal to the unit square [0,1] x [0,1] minus the removed square [0, 0.5] x [0.5, 1] (notch in the upper-left corner), with a re-entrant corner at (0.5, 0.5).
Mesh: unstructured/structured mesh of the L-shaped domain with 64 elements per edge of the unit square; unit thickness.
Material: linear elastic, isotropic, with E = 70e9 Pa, nu = 0.33, density rho = 2700 kg/m^3, and gravity g = 9.81 m/s^2.
Use the reduced plane-stress constitutive law with unit thickness.
Use a vector-valued displacement space of continuous Lagrange elements of order 1 (P1), i.e. VectorFunctionSpace(mesh, "Lagrange", 1).
Apply gravity as a volumetric body load (rho * g acting in the -y direction) over the whole domain.
Apply the traction only on the full outer right edge x = 1, y in [0, 1], as a vertical component t_y = sigma_yy(y) = -2.65e4 * y Pa, evaluated with the y-coordinate of the point on the loaded boundary; t_x = 0 on that edge. Do not evaluate the profile with the global x-coordinate.
At y = 0 the traction is 0 Pa; at y = 1 the traction is -2.65e4 Pa (compressive, pointing in -y).
Leave the re-entrant inner boundaries of the notch traction-free: the face x = 0.5 for y in [0.5, 1] and the face y = 0.5 for x in [0, 0.5].
Clamp (u = 0) the left boundary x = 0 on the remaining segment y in [0, 0.5].
Assemble the weak form with the plane-stress reduced stiffness and solve the linear system with a direct solver (e.g. LU via "mumps" or default direct method).
Compute the Cauchy in-plane stress field (sigma_xx, sigma_yy, tau_xy) from the P1 displacement field (e.g. via a DG0 or P1 stress projection consistent with dolfin legacy).
Compute the von Mises stress from the in-plane Cauchy stress components.
Output the displacement field (magnitude and components) and the von Mises stress distribution over the L-shaped domain.
